q: How do I create a filter?
steps: Go to Configuration › Events › Filters.
Clone a filter that is close to what you want, or click Add.
Name it TRAIN_yourinitials_… and set User Owner to yourself, so it stays private.
Type the condition in Filter Clause, for example Severity >= 4 AND Ack = 0.
Choose a Default Display so the right columns load with it.
Save, go to Events and pick it from the Filter dropdown.
note: A filter only changes what you see. It cannot change or delete an alarm.

q: How do I write the filter clause?
where: Filter Clause box of a filter
steps: Each condition is a field, a test and a value: Severity >= 4.
Text values need single quotes: Node = 'TST1_001'.
Use LIKE with % for any text: Node LIKE 'RAN1%'.
AND needs both, OR needs either. Put brackets round the OR part when you mix them.
Load it and check the number of alarms is what you expect.

q: How do I share a filter with a team?
where: Configuration › Events › Filters, then Filter Groups
steps: Use the filter yourself for a shift first.
Show a senior admin and agree the name and which group it belongs in.
Set User Owner to “Public to All Users In Group” and choose the Group Owner.
Open Configuration › Events › Filter Groups and add the filter to the team’s group.
Ask someone in that team to confirm it appears and shows the right alarms.
note: Only public filters can go in a group. Changing a filter back to private removes it from every group.

q: How do I limit a team to its own alarms?
steps: Go to Configuration › Events › Filter Groups and expand Global.
Select the group the team uses.
Write the extra condition, for example Node LIKE 'RAN1%'.
That condition is added with AND to every filter in the group.
Load a shared filter as that team and check the count.
note: A restriction changes what a whole team can see. Agree any change first.

q: How do I create or change a display?
steps: Go to Configuration › Events › Displays.
Clone a display close to what you want and name it TRAIN_yourinitials_….
Tick Visible for each column you want.
Set a Custom Name for a friendlier header and a Width (a number, or flex:2).
Drag fields into Sorting order for the default sort.
Save, then choose it in the Display dropdown on the event list.
note: A filter needs the real Field name, not the Custom Name shown in the header.

q: Why did an alarm disappear from my list?
steps: If your filter has Ack = 0, an acknowledged alarm drops out. Load a filter without it.
A clear sets Severity 0 and the row is deleted a few minutes later.
A Count, time or node condition may no longer match.
A filter group’s Restriction Filter may be hiding it.
Search Discover for the node: cleared alarms live on there.

q: How do I acknowledge and take ownership of an alarm?
where: Events, right-click tools menu on a row
steps: Click the alarm in the event list.
Use the Acknowledge tool. Ack becomes 1.
Use Take Ownership so OwnerName shows your user.
Write what you are doing, so the next shift can read it.
If your filter has Ack = 0, the row now drops out. That is expected.

q: How do I set up a new alarm?
steps: Look for it arriving as Unknown, and note its exact text and Method.
In Configuration › Rules, open the rules the receiving aggregator loads.
Add a condition that recognises the text.
Set Severity, EventType and Summary.
Node + SubNode + EventType, so repeats count instead of flooding.
Send a test message and check one clean row appears. Rules are version-controlled, so it can be rolled back.
note: A syntax error in rules can stop an aggregator processing. Make your first changes with a senior admin.

q: How do I change the severity of an alarm?
steps: On the alarm, read which source and rule set handled it.
In Configuration › Rules, find the file named after the SubMethod.
Search for a word from the Summary, then the line that sets Severity.
Change the value with a senior admin. The save is a new revision.
New alarms arrive with the new severity. Existing rows keep theirs.
note: A filter cannot change severity. It can only choose which rows to show.

q: How do I stop one alarm filling the list with duplicates?
steps: Expand two of the duplicate rows and compare their EventKey.
A time, sequence number or counter in the key makes every message look new.
In the rule, build the key from Node + SubNode + EventType only.
The next repeats should raise Count on one row.

q: Why does an alarm not clear when the fault is fixed?
where: Configuration › Rules, then Configuration › Events › Mechanizations
steps: Look for the clear message: Severity 0, EventCategory 1.
Node, SubNode and EventType must be identical on the clear and the problem.
If one differs, the rules label the clear wrongly. That is a rules fix.
If all three match, check the pairing mechanization is enabled and running.

q: How do I create a threshold alarm?
steps: Go to Configuration › Metrics › Thresholds.
Choose the measurement, for example CPU utilisation.
Set the test and value: above 85%.
Require several polls in a row, so one spike does not alarm.
Choose the severity the alarm is raised with.
Assign it to a small group of devices first and watch for a day.

q: How do I search alarm history?
steps: Go to Analytics › Events › Discover.
The index pattern at top left should be eventanalytics-*.
Set the time picker to Last 24 hours or longer.
Use field : value, for example Node : RAN1_* and Severity >= 4.
Click Add beside the fields you want as columns.
Save the search as TRAIN_yourinitials_….

q: How do I count alarms per node or source?
steps: Go to Analytics › Events › Administration › Console.
Type GET eventanalytics-*/_search and a JSON body.
Add a query, for example a range on @timestamp from now-7d.
Add a terms aggregation on the field to group by, such as Node.
Set "size": 0 so only the counts come back.
Press the green arrow or Ctrl+Enter.
note: Use GET only. PUT, POST and DELETE can change or remove history.

q: How do I find out why a search is slow?
steps: It is the tab beside the Console.
Change Index from _all to eventanalytics-*.
Paste only the JSON body of the query, without the GET line.
Click Profile and expand the Query Profile tree.
A wildcard at the front of a value is the usual culprit. Narrow the time range first.

q: Why is a field missing in Discover?
where: Analytics › Events › Administration › Management › Index Patterns
steps: In Management, under Kibana, open Index Patterns.
Select the pattern to see every field and its type.
Click the refresh button. This is safe and routinely needed.
Reload Discover; the field is now in the list.

q: Which screen do I use for what?
where: Search Configs, at the top of the left menu
steps: Filters, Filter Groups and Displays, under Configuration › Events.
Configuration › Rules.
Configuration › Metrics › Thresholds.
Configuration › Events › Mechanizations.
Analytics › Events: Discover, Console, Search Profiler.
Type the name into Search Configs at the top of the left menu.

q: What is safe for me to change?
steps: Change a copy of a shared filter or display.
Name practice items TRAIN_yourinitials_….
Stay as User Owner until it has been reviewed.
Filters, displays, Discover and GET queries only read.
Rules, mechanizations, services, and anything under Elasticsearch management.
Keep a note of what you changed and why.

q: How do I remove my practice items?
where: Configuration › Events › Filters and Displays; Management › Saved Objects
steps: Search for TRAIN_yourinitials in Filters and in Displays.
Delete only items where you are the User Owner.
Then the displays they used.
In Kibana Management › Saved Objects, export, then delete your TRAIN_ searches.
Record what you removed.
